Definition: Users focus on one thing and miss everything else
Design Implication: Don't rely on peripheral elements for important info

Definition: People miss changes outside their focus area
Design Implication: Animate or highlight changes explicitly

Definition: Users ignore anything that looks like an ad
Design Implication: Don't put important content in ad-shaped containers

Definition: Focused users miss unexpected elements
Design Implication: Critical actions must be in the expected flow

Definition: Close elements are perceived as grouped
Design Implication: Spacing IS meaning — related items tight unrelated separated

Definition: Similar-looking elements are perceived as related
Design Implication: Consistent styling for similar functions

Definition: Items in a shared container feel grouped
Design Implication: Cards borders and backgrounds create implicit relationships

Definition: People complete incomplete shapes mentally
Design Implication: Progress bars and partial reveals leverage this

Definition: Eyes follow lines and curves naturally
Design Implication: Align elements along clear visual paths

Definition: Foreground separates from background instantly
Design Implication: Contrast and layering create depth and hierarchy

Definition: Visual connections bind elements
Design Implication: Timelines and flow diagrams leverage explicit connections

Definition: Elements moving together are perceived as grouped
Design Implication: Coordinated animations signal relationship

Definition: Working memory holds ~7 chunks
Design Implication: Keep nav items and option lists under 7

Definition: Grouped information is easier to process
Design Implication: Break data into digestible groups

Definition: Showing options beats asking users to remember
Design Implication: Dropdowns beat free text; visual menus beat text lists

Definition: Every element demands mental processing
Design Implication: Remove anything that doesn't serve the current task

Definition: Prior exposure influences interpretation
Design Implication: What users see first colors everything after

Definition: Experiences judged by peak moment and ending
Design Implication: Invest in best moment and last moment of any flow

Definition: Users remember where things are on screen
Design Implication: Don't move navigation or key actions between visits

Definition: Images remembered better than words
Design Implication: Key concepts benefit from visual representation

Definition: Unfinished tasks nag more than completed ones
Design Implication: Progress indicators pull users back

Definition: Improvement is steep early then plateaus
Design Implication: First-time experiences matter most

Definition: Users approach interfaces with pre-existing expectations
Design Implication: Match common patterns before innovating

Definition: Users follow links that smell like what they want
Design Implication: Labels must clearly describe the destination

Definition: Users assess cost vs reward before clicking
Design Implication: If path to value looks expensive users bail

Definition: More choices equals longer decision time
Design Implication: Reduce options to essentials

Definition: Users pick the first acceptable option
Design Implication: Put best option where they'll see it first

Definition: Losing hurts ~2x more than gaining
Design Implication: Frame around what they'll miss not just what they gain

Definition: First number seen sets reference point
Design Implication: Show high-value metric or price first

Definition: Most users never change defaults
Design Implication: Set defaults to best outcome for the user

Definition: Larger closer targets are faster to click
Design Implication: Primary CTAs large and near current focus

Definition: 0.1s instant 1s responsive 10s loses attention
Design Implication: Skeleton screens for anything over 1s

Definition: Every click scroll keypress is a cost
Design Implication: Minimize steps to complete any action

Definition: People need autonomy competence and relatedness
Design Implication: Let users choose help them succeed connect them to others

Definition: New time periods motivate new commitments
Design Implication: Monday and first of month are optimal for prompts

Definition: Unpredictable rewards are more engaging
Design Implication: Daily-varying content creates habit loops

Definition: Internal motivation outlasts rewards
Design Implication: Build products people want to use not products that bribe usage

Definition: People seek info that confirms beliefs
Design Implication: Present balanced information; highlight unexpected wins

Definition: First info disproportionately influences judgment
Design Implication: Lead with strongest stat or testimonial

Definition: Recent events feel more common
Design Implication: Recent successes displayed prominently feel stronger

Definition: Negative experiences weigh heavier
Design Implication: One bad experience can erase ten good ones

Definition: One positive attribute colors all perception
Design Implication: Beautiful design makes content feel more credible

Definition: Designers assume users think like they do
Design Implication: Test with real users — your intuition is usually wrong

Definition: Presentation changes interpretation
Design Implication: Same data framed differently creates different impact

Definition: Time invested makes people reluctant to leave
Design Implication: Users who've customized settings or saved data feel invested

Definition: People overvalue what they have
Design Implication: Free trials work because taking something away feels like loss

Definition: Give value before asking for anything
Design Implication: Free content or tools earn trust before payment request

Definition: People follow what others do in uncertainty
Design Implication: Real numbers outperform vague claims

Definition: Limited availability increases perceived value
Design Implication: Only use when genuinely scarce — never fake it

Definition: Expertise signals increase trust
Design Implication: Track records and methodology transparency build credibility

Definition: People trust those they relate to
Design Implication: Brand personality and conversational tone increase connection

Definition: Small commitments lead to larger ones
Design Implication: Free action then account then payment — each step natural

Definition: Users notice then judge
Design Implication: Credibility signals must be visible not buried

Definition: Trust builds through 5 levels
Design Implication: Don't ask for the sale at level 1 — earn each level

Definition: Personalization has a boundary
Design Implication: Helpful recommendations good — surveillance-style messaging bad

Definition: Visceral-Behavioral-Reflective
Design Implication: Design must work at all three levels

Definition: Beautiful things feel easier to use
Design Implication: Visual polish improves perceived usability

Definition: Surface delight and deep delight both matter
Design Implication: Deep delight (goal completion) outweighs surface animation

Definition: Formed in 50ms and color all subsequent experience
Design Implication: First screen must earn trust instantly

Definition: People attribute personality to conversational systems
Design Implication: Conversational interfaces create emotional connection

Definition: Finishing a task is inherently rewarding
Design Implication: Celebrate completions — don't just move on

Definition: Persuasion respects autonomy — manipulation removes it
Design Implication: Stay on the persuasion side of the bright line

Definition: Users should understand what they agree to
Design Implication: Clear pricing honest records visible terms

Definition: Users should be able to undo decisions
Design Implication: Easy unsubscribe easy settings change no punitive flows
